What better place to start than with the classic Ravenloft-I6!

I6 Ravenloft (AD&D 1st Edition) was written by Tracy and Laura Hickman and published by TSR, Inc. in 1983. Designed for character levels 5–7, it became one of the most iconic adventures in Dungeons & Dragons history.

Choose a location to begin exploring Barovia.

Faithful to the Map. Open to Imagination.

We take the original maps seriously: their roads, landmarks, rooms, and connections deserve painstaking care. But our visual world is deliberately stylized. The village, trees, swirling fog, and monsters offer enough detail to awaken a picture in your mind without deciding every detail for you. We build the world; your imagination completes it.

Traditional gameplay, preserved

DNDPOV handles 3D exploration, location descriptions, conditional and random encounter checks, and surprise announcements. You keep character decisions, roleplaying, combat, initiative, attack and damage rolls at the table. No platform-specific module edition or complicated campaign setup is required.

How DNDPOV works

Your adventure. Your rules. Your point of view. DNDPOV is a first-person exploration companion—not a video game or a replacement for the original adventure module.

What DNDPOV handles

  • Walkable 3D environments, ambient sound, and interactive maps with visited-area tracking.
  • Location-based boxed descriptions and optional DM-only instructions.
  • Automatic location-based, conditional, and random encounter checks where implemented.
  • Surprise announcements identifying creatures or events and prompting players to roll initiative when appropriate.

What stays at the table

  • Character choices, conversations, roleplaying, and storytelling.
  • Combat, initiative order, hit points, attacks, saving throws, and damage.
  • Your own dice, characters, rules, and Dungeon Master.
  • Your original adventure materials; DNDPOV is a companion, not a substitute for the module.

Choose your experience

Text ON/OFF shows or hides room descriptions and inline DM notes. Encounters ON/OFF enables automatic encounter checks and surprise alerts. DM ON/OFF reveals or hides DM-only instructions and encounter summaries. Visited Map ON/OFF shows or hides explored-area highlights.

No virtual tabletop campaign to configure and no platform-specific edition to purchase just to use the walkthrough. Launch in your browser and explore. You can also use a local copy with the required assets. Speechify narration is optional and controlled separately through Speechify.

How to play

Use DND POV on your own or bring it to your next group session.

Solo adventurers

  1. Use ChatGPT as your Dungeon Master and upload the adventure module to your chat.
  2. Use Speechify to listen to the narration if you prefer an audio experience.
  3. Open DND POV and walk through the environment as the story unfolds.

Videos are loaded from the /videos folder.

Recommended solo setup: ChatGPT Dungeon Master + uploaded module + Speechify + DND POV.

Group adventures — multiplayer

Start the local multiplayer server, host as DM, and have players join with the session code. Everyone moves independently and appears on the shared minimap.

Explore together while your Dungeon Master runs the session. DNDPOV can automatically check and announce encounters, but your group still controls decisions, roleplaying, dice rolls, and combat.

Your group keeps control of the story, decisions, encounters, and dice rolls.

Map Accuracy & Attention to Detail

One village. Two perspectives. An adventure brought to life.

Compare the branching streets, central square, church and cemetery, and the road toward the eastern entrance.
Step into the Village of Barovia →

Original adventure cartography shown for visual comparison; rights remain with the original rights holders. Screenshot from DNDPOV v5.51.

Faithfulness to the original adventure maps is at the heart of DNDPOV. We are not simply creating settings inspired by classic Dungeons & Dragons adventures. We are painstakingly recreating their maps as fully explorable, first-person 3D worlds.

Every road, landmark, building, room, passage, staircase, and connection is carefully considered against the source material. Our attention to detail is intended to make these places instantly recognizable to veteran players while allowing new adventurers to experience them from ground level.

Village of Barovia: The village has been meticulously reconstructed from the original adventure map, closely preserving its streets, building placements, relative spacing, and important landmarks. The Blood of the Vine Tavern, Bildrath's Mercantile, Mad Mary's House, the Burgomaster's Mansion, church, and cemetery stand in their recognizable locations within a continuous, walkable village.

Lands of Barovia: The Old Svalich Road, Gates of Barovia, river crossings, journey to Tser Pool, and approach to Castle Ravenloft follow the original adventure's routes and geographical relationships with exceptional care. The aim is to let players travel the same legendary paths, rather than merely visit disconnected scenic recreations.

Castle Ravenloft: Our most intricate reconstruction follows the original floor plans with close attention to individual rooms, corridors, doors, staircases, and the complex connections between levels. The complete castle is mapped in our development build; the public beta currently offers the main floor.

Faithful Maps, Immersive Worlds

Translating a two-dimensional module map into a walkable three-dimensional environment requires decisions about heights, textures, terrain, lighting, vegetation, and atmosphere. Our artistic license is primarily in how these places look and feel—not in casually rearranging the maps that define them. Where practical adjustments are necessary, preserving the original layout and sense of place remains our priority.

We want longtime fans to recognize the architecture and geography they remember, and new players to feel they have stepped into the adventure itself.

Accurate by Design. Abstract on Purpose.

Accuracy and photorealism are different goals. We pay close attention to the original adventure's geography and architecture while deliberately leaving room for interpretation in its appearance. Our trees, buildings, weather, and creatures suggest a world rather than supply one final, definitive image of it.

Take the trees along the Old Svalich Road. They aren't photorealistic, but their layered branches and dark silhouettes feel like the woods of Barovia. That feeling is more important than rendering every leaf. We provide the forest's shape and mood; your imagination makes it a place.

Think of a character you pictured while reading a novel. Seeing an actor or a portrait can replace that private image forever. A perfectly rendered monster can do much the same thing. But a suggestive, abstract creature gives you its silhouette, its movement, and its menace—and then your own imagination supplies the face in the darkness. That act of filling in what isn't shown is part of the magic of tabletop role-playing. We want DNDPOV to preserve it, not take it away.

We bring the maps to life. You play the adventure.

Dungeon Design Inspiration & Credits

Our Castle Ravenloft dungeon draws significant visual and architectural inspiration from the beautifully detailed maps created by DM Andy (Andy Maps). His remarkable interpretations have been invaluable references in translating the castle's architecture into a first-person world.

We have taken great care to preserve the rooms, corridors, staircases, floor layouts, and intricate relationships between the castle's levels while adding our own lighting, materials, environmental details, and atmosphere. This work is a tribute to the imagination and craftsmanship of the original adventure and the artists who have brought it to life.

Special thanks to DM Andy for his outstanding map artwork and contribution to the Dungeons & Dragons community. Explore the reference maps below and visit his Castle Ravenloft map pack.
